about: Edge cases of Portuguese syllabification. Every accepted split names the sources that give it; a word may have more than one. Splits use the engine's notation: a hyphen stays on the syllable it ends.

The u is a nucleus in the base adjective in -uo or -ue: Mateus & d'Andrade 1998 p. 20 write that a [+high] segment before a [-high] vowel 'is perceived by Portuguese speakers as syllabic, that is, a vowel and not a glide', and p. 21 that such segments 'are syllable nuclei at the base level'.
